To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the hand paths of joint planar reaching movement are adapted so as not to be straight lines in Cartesian (physical) space but rather in perceived space.

(i) reaching movements in the horizontal are adapted so as as to produce straight paths in perceived space, (ii) this adaptation can be achieved by changing the movement trajectory, and (iii) this adaptation is observed even when the motion is perceived in Cartesian space.
Reaching movements are planned in visually perceived space, and are adapted so as as to produce straight line paths in visually perceived space."
In summary, our research is concerned with
the nature and origin of motor commands that are generated to guide reaching movements.
the nature of the spatial reference frame that is used for the planning and control of visually guided reaching movements.
the nature of the spatial frame of reference used by the motor system to plan reaching movements.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the planning and control of visually guided reaching movements is performed in a perceptual reference frame.
reaching movements are planned within a frame of reference that is based on visual perception.
the trajectory of a reaching movement is adapted so as to result in a straight line in visually perceived space.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the visual system is able to extract a perceptual frame in which the movement is planned and executed.
the visuomotor system is adapted to the nonlinear visuomotion transformation, and that the adaptation is achieved by the motion planning process.
reaching movements are planned on the basis of visual perception, and the visual system is adapted to the task demands.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the brain is able to adapt to nonlinear distortions of the visuomotor system, such that the planning of visually guided movements is performed in a visually perceived frame of reference.
we have demonstrated that visuomotor transformations can be adapted in real-time to a nonlinear visuo-spatial transformation.
the brain is capable of learning and executing complex motor actions in perceptual rather than Cartesian space.
